label: Experiment
doc: An experiment is an object whose CONTRACT is frozen and whose state is not.
Everything under `contract` is pre-registration: what was going to be
measured, on which units, against which split, for how long, decided before
any data was seen. The readout reads the contract rather than its own
request arguments, which is what makes the primary question un-switchable
after the fact. Everything outside `contract` is live state and moves.
This is also what makes an experiment reviewable by somebody who was not
there: 'you registered conversion at 14 days and are reading revenue at
day 6' is a mechanical comparison, not a judgement call.

lift.description: LAST OBSERVED lift, cached so a list of 240 rows does not run 240 readouts. Not authoritative and never a basis for a decision: `experiments.readout` recomputes it, applies the sample-ratio gate, and is the only thing that may be acted on. Paired with lift_at so staleness is visible rather than implied.

better.description: Which way the cached lift is good, carried from the metric the last recorded readout cited.

srm_passed.description: Whether the last recorded readout's sample-ratio check passed. Null when it could not run.

last_readout.description: The most recently recorded readout object. A decision cites a readout; this is the default one.

started_at.description: When traffic really started, set by experiments.start. Every readout of a started experiment reads from here, not from 'the last 30 days'. For an experiment registered while already running this is in the past.

stopped_at.description: When it stopped, set by experiments.stop or experiments.decide. Readouts read up to here and no further.

decision.description: What was decided, by whom, and on which recorded readout. Written only by experiments.decide, alongside a decision object in the graph.

contract.description: Pre-registration, frozen at start. The readout resolves these instead of trusting the caller, so the primary metric cannot be swapped after the numbers are visible.

unit.description: Column the experiment randomised on. Without it every count counts ROWS, which makes intervals too narrow and inflates the sample-ratio statistic.

weights.description: The DESIGNED split, arm -> weight. Required for anything but an even split: a deliberate 90/10 holdout checked against an assumed 50/50 fails its sample-ratio check every time.

metric_version.description: PINNED. A dashboard cites a metric id and follows the current ratified meaning, which is right for 'what is our refund rate now'. An experiment must not: if the definition is re-ratified mid-flight, the readout would answer a different question from the registered one. So this pins the version in force at registration.

guardrails.description: Frozen too — a guardrail added after seeing data was not pre-registered.

mde.description: Minimum effect worth detecting, as a RELATIVE fraction — 0.02 means a 2% lift, on the same scale as the readout's `lift`, not 2 percentage points. Not used in the arithmetic; it is what makes 'no difference detected' readable as underpowered rather than as flat.

unit_agg.description: How a unit's several rows collapse to one observation. Frozen, because it decides what the number IS: revenue per user summed and revenue per user averaged are different experiments.

cap.description: Winsorise each unit's value before aggregating. Frozen — choosing a cap after seeing which outliers landed in which arm is p-hacking with extra steps.

null_is_zero.description: Whether a unit with no matching outcome rows counts as zero. For revenue per exposed user it does: they were exposed and spent nothing. For a latency guardrail where a null means missing instrumentation it does not, and imputing zero understates by however much is missing.

sequential.description: Whether the interval is always-valid — an anytime confidence sequence rather than a fixed-horizon t interval. FROZEN, because it is the error-control regime and not a way of looking at the evidence. Read at n=10,000 with 1000 vs 1089 conversions, the sequence gives (-0.052, +0.230) and the fixed interval (+0.0005, +0.177): the same data, 'no difference detected' and 'better'. Choosing after seeing which one says 'better' is the whole thing pre-registration prevents.

tuning.description: The sample size the confidence sequence is tightest at. FROZEN for the same reason as `sequential`: it sets the width of the interval, and an interval whose width is chosen after the data is not a guarantee about anything.

threshold.description: The p below which the split is called broken. FROZEN. It is not a reading choice: an SRM failure overrides the verdict with 'no answer', so a threshold chosen afterwards is a way to make the override go away. 0.001 by default, not 0.05 — this is a check run on every readout, and at 0.05 one experiment in twenty is condemned for nothing.
